messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — elevated 5xx and request latency in eu-west-1 for Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Alert source: edge-proxy and runtime metrics. Possible root: observability ingest errors (third-party logs provider). See: https://status.thirdeye-logs.com/incident/482

incident-bot: Symptom summary: increased 5xx at api-gateway (500/502 spikes), per-token latency up from 120ms -> 450ms, key error: upstream obs-forwarder 429/503. Pager sent to #incidents on-call.

erin: oncall here — acknowledged. Starting triage. Is this region-only? any customer-reported impacts?

matt: looking at provider status and our proxy traces — ThirdEye Logs is returning 503s and intermittent 429s for the log-ingest endpoint in eu-west-1. Link: https://status.thirdeye-logs.com/notes

matt: sample error from edge proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:04:12Z api-gw eu-west-1 obs-forwarder: upstream 503 "service unavailable" attempt=3 conn=12
2026-03-15T10:04:13Z runtime eu-west-1: kv-cache write timeout, backlog=324
```

sam: yep, seeing large backlog in obs-forwarder connection pool. It's synchronous on request path for a subset of telemetry (request tracing + debug logs) — when it stalls the request threads wait and we get timeout/5xx. Dedicated pools with telemetry enabled are showing similar thread starvation.

erin: immediate mitigations?

sam: two quick levers: 1) flip feature flag to stop forwarding non-critical logs/traces in eu-west-1, 2) enable circuit-breaker (fail open) on obs-forwarder so we short-circuit to sampling. I can push both.

erin: do it. Post the commands here and we can run a quick smoke.

sam: running feature-flag toggle now:
```
# toggle non-critical forwarding in region
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \
  https://config.redwood.internal/flags/obs_forwarder_non_critical -d '{"eu-west-1": false}'
```

ops-bot: command accepted, change-id `cfg-5912`, queued for region roll.

matt: I'm going to enable the circuit-breaker on the obs-forwarder proxy in eu-west-1 to return 202 for sampled telemetry and drop heavy payloads. Applying now.

deploy-bot: rolling config change `cfg-5912` to eu-west-1 (canary 2 nodes -> full). Logs: success on canary.

matt: circuit-breaker is active. Observability forwarder now returning 202 for sampled payloads. Monitoring for request latency.

erin: metrics update?

matt: within 90s we see API 5xx rate drop ~70%, median latency down to 160ms. A few dedicated pools still elevated — looks like some processes are still draining their backlog.

julia: support note draft: "We're investigating elevated errors/latency in eu-west-1 due to third-party log provider degradation. We've applied temporary mitigations to reduce load; requests should be returning to normal. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem." Want me to post to status.redwood.ai?

erin: yes, post and tag impacted customers. Use Sev2 classification for now.

julia: posting to status and sending customer advisory to impacted Dedicated pool owners.

sam: for Dedicated pools: enabling dedicated telemetry path to internal-batched-sink for affected customers — this prevents them from hitting the shared obs-forwarder. Doing now.

ops-bot: ran job `telemetry-reroute-2026-03-15` for 6 dedicated pools in eu-west-1 — success on 5/6, one failing due to config mismatch (pool id dp-42).

matt: I'll patch dp-42 config and reroute manually.

matt: dp-42 reroute complete. No more thread starvation observed.

erin: handing off to jordan for follow-up and postmortem. Summary for handoff:
- root cause: ThirdEye Logs degraded ingest in eu-west-1 returning 429/503 -> caused obs-forwarder backlog and upstream request thread starvation -> 5xx/latency spikes on API and Dedicated pools (telemetry synchronous path).
- mitigations performed: toggled non-critical forwarding off (`cfg-5912`), enabled circuit-breaker for obs-forwarder, rerouted Dedicated telemetry to internal-batched-sink for impacted pools, scaled down forwarder connection pool drain windows.
- customer impact: ~12% of requests in region got 5xx at peak, some Dedicated customers experienced elevated latency/errors for ~8 minutes, support notifications sent.
- next steps: postmortem, vendor escalation with ThirdEye, permanent change to make obs-forwarder async and non-blocking for request path.

jordan: taking over. Thanks erin/sam/matt. I'll create the incident folder and schedule a 1h follow-up in 30m to capture timeline and action items. Assigning postmortem owners: sam (runtime), matt (infra), julia (customer comms).

jordan: will open a vendor support ticket and request RTO/RPO details & timeline from ThirdEye. Please drop any logs/traces into incident thread.

erin: +1. Great work. Closing immediate page.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial recovery). Severity: updated to Sev2. Follow-up meeting scheduled at 10:40 UTC.

julia: preparing concise customer update to send after follow-up meeting.

jordan: end-handoff notes saved to /incidents/2912345678/notes.txt — will add timeline and commands used.

erin: recommended long-term actions to include in postmortem: decouple obs-forwarder from request path, enable async fire-and-forget by default, add regional circuit-breaker and vendor failover for telemetry, and add dedicated-pool telemetry isolation policy.

sam: will draft a remediation PR and link it in the postmortem.

jordan: thanks all, unpaging now. :thumbsup:
